record.paper_title: Singularity Theorems in General Relativity: Achievements and Open Questions.
record.original_question: How should singularities in general relativity be given a rigorous mathematical structure and set of properties, and what precise relationship, if any, should hold between geodesic incompleteness and curvature pathologies when singularities are defined by incomplete inextensible curves rather than by points inside the spacetime manifold?

evidence.quote: Some fundamental questions, which sometimes are omitted, arise at this point. How can one give structure and properties to the singularities? What is the relation between geodesic incompleteness and curvature problems, if any?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let (M, g) be a smooth, time-oriented, connected Lorentzian manifold (a spacetime). A singularity of (M, g) is conventionally identified not with a point of M but with the existence of an inextensible causal or timelike geodesic γ : [0, a) → M (with a ≤ ∞) that has finite affine length and cannot be extended to a larger parameter interval within any isometric extension of (M, g); such a γ is called an incomplete inextensible curve.

(a) Propose a rigorous mathematical framework that endows the collection of singularities of an arbitrary spacetime with the structure of a well-defined set (or space) and equips that set with intrinsic properties (e.g. a topology, a notion of locality, invariants such as a curvature type or causal character), in a way that is invariant under isometries and reduces to the expected notions in standard examples (Schwarzschild, FLRW big bang, conical singularities, plane-wave parallelly-propagated curvature singularities, Taub–NUT-type quasi-regular singularities, etc.).

(b) Within this framework, determine the precise logical relationship between geodesic incompleteness and curvature pathologies. Specifically: characterize necessary and sufficient geometric conditions under which an incomplete inextensible causal geodesic γ must be accompanied by unbounded behavior of curvature scalars (a scalar polynomial curvature singularity) or by unbounded components of the Riemann tensor in a parallelly propagated frame along γ (a p.p. curvature singularity), and conversely identify the conditions under which curvature pathologies imply geodesic incompleteness. In particular, decide whether one can classify all incomplete inextensible curves into curvature singularities and quasi-regular (non-curvature) singularities by intrinsic invariants of the proposed structure.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of giving spacetime singularities a rigorous intrinsic structure (e.g. b-boundary, c-boundary, g-boundary, abstract boundary constructions) and clarifying the relationship between geodesic incompleteness and curvature blow-up remains an active foundational issue in mathematical general relativity. No single construction has been universally accepted, and examples (Taub–NUT, Misner, conical, plane-wave) show geodesic incompleteness need not imply scalar curvature blow-up. The problem is generally regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: The abstract boundary - a singularity classification
status_evidence.snippet: Scott and Szekeres introduce the abstract boundary to classify singular boundary points, indicating the b-boundary and g-boundary constructions have known deficiencies and no consensus exists.
status_evidence.claim: There is no universally accepted rigorous structure for singularities in GR.

status_evidence.title: Singularity theorems in General Relativity (review, Senovilla)
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews discuss that geodesic incompleteness does not in general imply curvature singularities and that classifying singularities remains an open program.
status_evidence.claim: Relationship between geodesic incompleteness and curvature pathologies is not settled.
